title: Payload Beacon: compact failure reconnaissance & retry composer
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Operators in the Redwood Console need a compact, fast way to understand a failed inference request and attempt a safe retry without leaving context. Existing large 'deep-dive' payload inspectors are powerful but heavy — they slow triage and make quick retries error-prone.

Goal: Design a lightweight, focused UI pattern (the 'Payload Beacon') that surfaces the essentials of a failed request in a single compact strip and exposes a minimal retry composer. The pattern should: 1) show error taxonomy and confidence, 2) highlight tokenized input/response diffs (KV / prefix), 3) indicate cost and latency impact, 4) provide a sandboxed retry composer with auto-redaction and parameter presets, and 5) integrate with rollouts/fallback policies so users can launch a canary retry or switch to a safe model variant.

Constraints: must fit as an embed inside existing Request Details page and as a collapsed 'peek' in the failed requests list. Must respect RBAC and audit logging. Must avoid sending unredacted PII to external editors — client-side redaction + mode flags required. Must not add blocking backend work (use existing retry endpoint plus new query params).

Users: Support engineers, on-call SREs, platform owners performing quick triage and low-risk retries during incidents or to validate suspected transient failures.
acceptance_criteria: Compact Beacon UI rendered in Request List and Request Details pages that summarizes error class, top-3 contributing signals, and cost/latency ballpark
Retry composer opens inline with pre-filled safe inputs and a prominent privacy redaction toggle
Retry options include: 'Canary (1 req)', 'Batch (up to N)', and 'Model Variant fallback' linked to rollout config
Audit events emitted for every retry with metadata (user, reason, model, variant) — design doc for fields attached
Accessible keyboard flow and screen-reader labels for the beacon and retry composer
Prototype validated in 3 design reviews with FE/BE and one customer shadowing session showing < 2 min median triage time
decisions: Use a single-line compact summary (Beacon) with expandable context to avoid cognitive overhead — avoided full inspector as first-touch
Inline retry uses existing POST /requests/:id/retry endpoint with query flags for 'canary' and 'redact' to minimize backend changes
Show a small 'cost delta' ETA computed client-side using token estimates; exact billing shown on the request detail page to avoid confusion
Privacy: default retry mode is 'redact mode' (client-side) except for users with forensic privileges; document enforced via RBAC checks
Accessibility: ensure color is not the only indicator for error class; add concise aria-labels and readable microcopy
tradeoffs: Compactness vs. depth: the beacon intentionally omits full model stack traces; deeper debugging still links to the full inspector
Client-side redaction reduces backend scope but requires careful UX cues to prevent false confidence about what was redacted
Showing cost estimates increases trust but may be slightly inaccurate for burst/quantization differences — we surface as 'approx.'
